_note: PLACEHOLDER DATA. Design principle (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-robot-reaction-bridge-design.md): valence picks the emotion FAMILY, arousal picks the intensity (1-3). Restricted to Ekman's core 7 emotions only (Anger, Contempt, Disgust, Fear, Happiness, Sadness, Surprise) -- no LOVE/SHAME/INTEREST. The core 7 skew heavily negative (5 negative, 1 positive, 1 ambiguous), so high and medium valence each only have ONE valid candidate -- HAPPINESS is the only positive option, SURPRISE the only non-positive/non-negative one -- there is no genuine second option for either without reintroducing a non-core-7 emotion. Low valence keeps 2 candidates (SADNESS, FEAR) since the core 7's negative skew actually supports variety there; deliberately NOT pairing in ANGER/CONTEMPT/DISGUST even though they're core-7 -- those read as hostile, wrong register for a robot meant to stay supportive even with critical feedback. Which candidate gets picked when a cell has more than one: config.EMOTION_LLM_SELECTION_ENABLED=false (default) always picks candidates[0]; =true lets an LLM pick based on actual answer content -- see emotion_bank.py. Single-candidate cells never call the LLM regardless of the flag, nothing to choose between.
